question.text: A sample contains a large number of nuclei. The probability that a nucleus in the sample will decay after four half-lives is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi></mfrac></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>b</mi></math> are least positive integers. Value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi></math> will be

solution.text:
The probability that a nucleus will not decay is-

NN0=12n=q

When n is the number of half-lives

q=124=116

The probability that a nucleus will decay is

p=1-q=1-116=1516
